1. Case 1: Supraglottic edema from e-cigarette burn injury
Stridor, increased work of breathing, and oxygen requirement began after the patient fell with an e-cigarette in his mouth. CT showed glottic and supraglottic swelling without fractures, and laryngoscopy revealed diffuse edema with mucosal sloughing, confirming supraglottic obstruction. Esophageal scar and antral ulceration support a caustic/thermal burn mechanism. Traumatic exposure, absent fractures, and no supporting infection evidence argue against infectious supraglottitis, so the obstruction is supraglottic edema from e-cigarette burn.
